- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent low trend.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply linear decay correction starting from day 1–3 (reduce by 0.5–1% per day).
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model may misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment momentum (e.g., if sentiment rises, forecast should trend up).
